My friends and I planned a picnic in the park last Sunday.
We checked the weather the night before, and it looked clear and sunny.
We were all excited for a relaxing afternoon outside.
I woke up early to prepare food for everyone.
I made sandwiches, cut fruit, and packed drinks into a bag.
Everything looked perfect and ready when I finally finished.
We arrived at the park around noon, right on time.
The sky was blue, and the sun felt warm on our faces.
We found a nice spot under a big tree and spread out our blanket.
We ate our sandwiches and talked for almost an hour together.
Everyone seemed happy, and the weather still looked completely fine.
No one thought about rain at all that day.
Then, without much warning, the sky started to change quickly.
Dark clouds moved in fast from one side.
Within minutes, the bright sky turned gray and heavy.
A few drops of rain fell, and we looked at each other with worried faces.
Before we could pack anything up, the rain came down much harder.
We grabbed our things as fast as we possibly could.
We ran toward a small shelter near the park entrance.
Our blanket was already wet, and half our food got left behind on the grass.
We arrived under the shelter, laughing and completely soaked from head to toe.
We stood there together, dripping water everywhere onto the ground.
One friend still held a sandwich in her hand, somehow still dry.
We all laughed at how fast everything had changed around us, from sunny sky to complete chaos in minutes.
The rain continued for almost twenty minutes without stopping.
We waited under the shelter and shared the last dry sandwich between four people.
It tasted better than any picnic food I remembered eating, maybe because we were all so hungry by then.
When the rain finally stopped, the sun came back out again.
Everything looked fresh and clean, but our picnic spot was still very wet.
We decided to go get pizza instead of finishing the picnic, since our blanket was completely useless by then.
We sat in a small pizza shop, still a little damp, and talked about the whole afternoon.
It didn't go as planned, but somehow it became a better memory than we expected.
Sometimes the rain makes the very best stories, better than any perfectly sunny day would have.
